demos.name: writes
demos.description: One S3 bucket + policy on a local Floci emulator — blue to green in five minutes. The default.

demos.name: k8s
demos.description: An nginx Deployment + Service on a throwaway k3d cluster — runtime children (Pods), field ownership, honest unobserved. Cluster persists across runs; scripts/local/local-down.sh removes it.

demos.name: flux-estate
demos.description: A GitOps estate: a Flux control plane (GitRepository + Kustomizations) plus two app projects, served as one composed estate — cross-stack sourceRef edges, estate-wide drift, and the namespace join that reads app-b where the control plane's targetNamespace puts it. k3d + Flux, no cloud. scripts/estate-down.sh removes the cluster.

demos.name: argo-estate
demos.description: The Argo CD mirror of flux-estate, declared only: an AppProject plus one Application per app project, served with the two apps as one composed estate — project edges from each Application to the AppProject it names, and each Application's destination namespace drawn as a box holding that app's objects. No cluster, no Argo install, no Docker.

demos.name: terraform-estate
demos.description: A multi-root Terraform estate, declared only: two roots applied separately (envs/prod and platform) plus the shared module both are built on — 37 cards boxed by root, module calls expanded into their own contents, and the two look-alike versions.tf files told apart. Shows what behold does NOT infer as clearly as what it draws: platform declares the KMS key and prod reads it back by alias, and no edge is drawn between them, because both ends carry the same unresolved interpolation (#381). Needs chant's terraform lexicon beside behold, which behold does not install: npm install --no-save @intentius/chant-lexicon-terraform @cdktf/hcl2json (the refusal names the exact line). No cloud, no Docker, no terraform binary.

demos.name: carve
demos.description: The peel walkthrough: a half-migrated estate — a chant project beside a Terraform one — scored by `chant carve advise`, then a six-step stepper that carves one S3 bucket across the line on camera (advise, pick, emit, bridge, handoff, done). Emit and bridge really run, into the demo copy; the destructive terraform commands stay yours to paste. No cloud, no Docker, no terraform binary.

demos.name: choudoufu-estate
demos.description: A tag-owned estate: four choudoufu estates (an OpenTofu fork whose ownership is two AWS tags) served composed — the terralith applied to a scratch floci, three team estates whose declared resources are the monolith's (every card `owned by` it, dashed to its card), a cross-estate data-source edge, and a move plan whose `live-mv` lines you run by hand while behold previews with -dry-run and reads the receipt. A card's colour is ownership, not "nothing changed": attribute drift is a separate plan read, opt-in through ⌘K → "Re-check live with plan". Docker + choudoufu (0.16.0+, or a build from main) on PATH; provider download on first init. scripts/choudoufu-down.sh removes the container.

demos.name: fountain
demos.description: The mature estate: self-hosted fountain (a real app) on a throwaway k3d cluster — tiers (try the ha tier picker), seams, drift, runtime Pods. Clones INTENTIUS/fountain-ops; ~5 minutes, mostly image pulls. `just down` in the clone removes the cluster.
